quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Driving slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at the same speed at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers get distracted. A defensive driver watches other drivers and anticipates problems before they happen.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look for other cars nearby. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers your plans. Never use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: ____ limit your focus, awareness, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only alcohol above the legal limit can

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol harms your focus, awareness, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills suffer even with small amounts of alcohol. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to get more distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see if another car is following too close. If so, slow down gradually and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because cars are following too closely.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians at any intersection without a traffic light. This applies whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes:
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where they must stop.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Use your turn signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, you should:

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very careful.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you don't startle or scare it.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a merge is ahead. Two lanes of traffic moving the same direction will become one lane.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to obey are called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. You can get a ticket if you don't follow them.

questions.question: Another driver is trying to pass your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal to the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming cars and slow down to let them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming cars and slow down to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when another car tries to pass you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and slow down so the passing car can move back into the right lane safely.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if you see both a green arrow and a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. You must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots.
Release the gas pedal and let your car slow before braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop safely. Release the gas pedal first to let your car slow down. Then press the brake gently so your brake lights come on and your car stops smoothly.

questions.question: When another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear to encourage them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you and a right lane is open, move over. If no right lane exists, slow down gradually when it is safe so they can pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb:

options.text: Is necessary only if other traffic is nearby.
Is good driving practice and required by law.
Is necessary only during the move, not before.
Is not necessary if you drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is good driving practice and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. The law requires this. Always signal before pulling away from the curb to tell other drivers your plans.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver should honk to show they are yielding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: If you and another car arrive at an intersection at the same time, yield to the car on your right. Wait until it is safe, then you can go.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Wait for the police to arrive.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note. Include your name, address, and an explanation of the accident.

questions.question: What color are signs that show the distance to the next highway exit?
questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Signs that show where you are going are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: You cannot pass on either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can cross the center to pass, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights at night, look:

options.text: At the center of the road
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look at the oncoming headlights, as the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Pull to the right side of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over on the right side.

questions.question: An arrow painted on the pavement means:

options.text: Drivers in that lane may move in the direction shown if they want to.
Drivers in that lane must move in that direction only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers in that lane must stop completely before moving in that direction.
Drivers in that lane must move in that direction while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must move in that direction while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the pavement tells drivers they must move in that direction. Follow any traffic signs or signals before moving in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves to the right and then to the left. Slow down to safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Usually slows your reaction time to hazards.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually slows your reaction time to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions make you react slower to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is always unsafe.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs warn of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs tell you to yield to trains. Do not try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass even if it is risky.
Traffic in these lanes moves in opposite directions.
You may pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass or change lanes if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season to drive in.
Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid before winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires help your vehicle grip slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter requires extra caution. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid before cold weather arrives. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: The "No zone" refers to:

options.text: Blind spots around trucks and buses.
A roadway with rules about stereo volume.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots around trucks and buses.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on all sides, in the rear, and in the front. Cars cannot be seen in these blind spots, called the "No zone."

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle in which situations?

options.text: When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: If you stop on the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on so other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. Pull off the road on a two-lane road and let vehicles pass. Only drive below the speed limit when necessary.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down and yield to pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: You see flashing signals at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when you see a flashing signal or lowered gate at a railroad crossing. Listen and look for an approaching train.
